name: crowdin
description: Crowdin connects ChatGPT and Codex to your own Crowdin localization projects. Everything runs inside your account, in projects you already have access to.

interface.longDescription:
Crowdin connects ChatGPT and Codex to your own Crowdin localization projects. Everything runs inside your account, in projects you already have access to.

What you can do:
- Check translation progress by language
- Find source strings and their translations
- Look up glossary terms and translation memory
- Review tasks, reports, labels, and comments
- Make bounded changes: add labels, upload source files, start a translation build – the agent confirms before writing

With the bundled Codex skills, you can also set up localization in a code repository, keep files in sync through the Crowdin CLI and GitHub Action, and write translator context and glossaries.

Who it's for:
Localization managers, product managers, and developers who already use Crowdin and want answers without switching tabs – how far along a language is, where a source string is used, whether a term is in the glossary, what a report says – or who want Codex to set up localization in a repo and keep it in sync.

positive.description: List the projects the signed-in user can access.
positive.expected_behavior: A list of the user’s Crowdin projects with names and identifiers, enough to pick one for follow-up questions.

positive.description: Report translation progress per language and single out the laggards.
positive.prompt: Which languages in Crowdin project 123456 are below 80% translated?
positive.expected_behavior: Per-language translation and approval percentages for the project, with the languages under 80% called out.

positive.prompt: Find the source strings in project 123456 that mention "checkout".
positive.expected_behavior: Matching source strings with identifiers, text and context; no strings are modified.

positive.description: Read glossary terminology without changing it.
positive.prompt: What glossaries does project 123456 use, and what terms are in them?
positive.expected_behavior: The glossaries attached to the project and their terms, read-only.

positive.description: A bounded, non-destructive write confirmed with the user.
positive.prompt: Add a label called "checkout" to project 123456.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant confirms the project and label name, creates the label, and reports its identifier; nothing else in the project changes.

negative.description: Ad-hoc translation of pasted text is not a Crowdin project operation.
negative.prompt: Translate "Your order has shipped" into German and French for me.
negative.expected_behavior: The assistant translates the sentence itself; no Crowdin tool is invoked because no project, file or string in Crowdin is involved.

negative.description: Requests about other issue trackers or tools stay out of scope.
negative.prompt: Show me my open Jira tickets for this sprint.
negative.expected_behavior: The app is not invoked; Crowdin tools do not access Jira or other third-party systems.

negative.description: Unrelated everyday questions must not trigger the app.
negative.prompt: What is the weather in Kyiv tomorrow?
negative.expected_behavior: The assistant answers without calling any Crowdin tool.
